external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal using vendor-issued credentials.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded supplier paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the organization's cloud account.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

processes.name: Supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: A service that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes the records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor's platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where the supplier compliance documents remain stored.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organization's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a landing bucket in our cloud account
data_stores.notes: The source says the nightly extract is encrypted end to end, while the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in the organization's cloud account into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

data_flows.name: Supplier uploads compliance paperwork to Supplier document portal
data_flows.description: Supplier uploads insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: Category manager reviews Supplier document portal
data_flows.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded supplier compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decisions

data_flows.name: Supplier document portal stores documents in Vendor's platform
data_flows.description: The portal stores uploaded supplier compliance documents in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance paperwork and staff contact details

data_flows.name: Vendor pushes nightly extract to Landing bucket
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a supplier data extract every night to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source says the extract is encrypted end to end, while the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is. The conflicting claims leave encryption in transit unknown.

data_flows.name: Supplier master service loads Landing bucket
data_flows.description: The supplier master service picks up and loads the supplier data extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: Supplier master service writes records to Supplier database
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes the extracted supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: Supplier
trust_boundaries.description: The supplier-controlled zone from which suppliers access the portal.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor's platform
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting zone containing the SaaS portal and stored supplier documents.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal is internet-facing because suppliers sign in and upload paperwork through it.
assumptions.basis: Suppliers are described as signing in to and uploading paperwork through the portal.

assumptions.assumption: The documents stored in the vendor's platform are confidential because they include compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The nightly extract in the landing bucket is confidential because it contains supplier data.
assumptions.basis: The landing bucket receives a supplier data extract.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database is confidential because it contains supplier records derived from staff contact details and compliance data.
assumptions.basis: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the database.
